title: Season 2, Ep 1: What a platform actually is
oneliner: The platform is the layer between infrastructure and applications - the cream in the cake - where shared services live so every team doesn't rebuild them.
says: Before the roles and responsibilities of an AI platform solution architect, you must understand what a platform is: the layer between infrastructure and application. His analogy: a cake where the bottom layer is infrastructure, the middle - the cream and chocolate cookies - is the platform layer, and the decoration on top is the application.
explained: The cake analogy encodes the season's whole argument. Infrastructure (the base) is undifferentiated - compute, storage, GPUs from Season 1. Applications (the decoration) are where business value shows. The platform in the middle is where leverage lives: build a capability once - model access, retrieval, prompts, evaluation - and every application team consumes it instead of rebuilding it badly in six different ways.

This is why the role exists as its own discipline. Infrastructure architects answer 'is it running?'; application architects answer 'does it solve the problem?'; platform architects answer 'are we building the same thing fifty times?' Season 2 is the answer to that question, service by service: MCP hub, multi-tenancy, prompt registry, agent SDK, RAG, evaluation, tool catalog.
takeaway: Platform = shared services between raw infrastructure and business apps. Its job is leverage: build once, govern centrally, let every team consume.
